title: Do Spatial Vision SAE Features Encode Relative Position or Absolute Position?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding position encoding in visual features is an interesting research question but the chain to a safety outcome is weak. Position-invariance is more relevant to model capability understanding than to preventing harm.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: ViT-Prisma provides patch-level caching. The experimental design (same object at different positions) is conceptually clean. But creating properly controlled image datasets and training the SAE requires careful setup. Medium compute is adequate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear metric (position-invariance score per feature) and a focused experiment. However, creating the controlled image dataset, running inference at multiple positions, and analyzing per-feature patterns is non-trivial. Achievable in 30 hours if scope is tightly managed.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
